clue.text: He wrote saucy stuff with affection and skill

parts.note: HP is a brand of brown sauce, a staple of British tables
love is warm affection
craft is skill, as in a craftsman's skill

explanation.surface: A writer of racy material who brings warmth and talent to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saucy stuff' looks like smut but points to HP Sauce, a British brown sauce. The writer is the American horror author, who wrote nothing saucy.
explanation.definitionFit: The American horror writer of the Cthulhu stories is a man who wrote, so 'He wrote' fits him.

clue.text: Like a certain baroness, attacks witches hanging around with baron

indicators.note: hanging around something means surrounding it, so these letters go round the others

parts.note: hags are witches
and means with, joining things together

explanation.surface: A baroness launching attacks while surrounded by witches and a baron.
explanation.walkthrough: The baroness is Margaret Thatcher, famous for swinging her handbag at ministers, which gave British English the verb 'to handbag'.
explanation.definitionFit: To handbag, from Thatcher's style, is to attack verbally and forcefully, so the phrase describes the Thatcher kind of attacks.

clue.text: Every five years, there's passion with return of the French right

parts.note: lust is strong passion

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: la is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Something that comes round every five years, bringing passion and a revival of French conservatism.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrum was the Roman five-yearly purification, so the adjective can mean happening at five-year intervals.

clue.text: Occasionally I've eyed Rose in slacks

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Now and then the speaker has admired a woman called Rose wearing trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slacks' looks like trousers but is a verb: in sailing, to veer a rope is to let it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautically, letting out a cable or rope gradually is a synonym for slackening it.

clue.text: Charles is snatching old Bob's body

indicators.note: snatching something means grabbing and holding it, so these letters take the other in

parts.note: Chas is the short form of the name Charles
taken as written
a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: Someone called Charles grabbing the corpse of an old man named Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' is not a name but slang for the pre-decimal British shilling, whose symbol was s.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's chassis is its frame or body, the structure the rest is mounted on.

clue.text: Witty article on reflection

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
musing is reflection, quiet thought

explanation.surface: A clever, funny article written about thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something witty is entertaining and makes people laugh, which is the synonym sense here.

clue.text: Italian poet has very big day coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday

explanation.surface: An Italian poet has an important day ahead of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the sixteenth-century Italian epic poet of Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Terms of Tommy Lee Jones's agreement

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so the final letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: The conditions of a contract signed by the actor Tommy Lee Jones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' looks like contract conditions but means termini, endings.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the word is giving agreement, an affirmative reply.

clue.text: One addressed German prince in Irish resort

parts.note: the person spoken to is called you
Hal is Prince Henry in Shakespeare's Henry IV

explanation.surface: A letter addressed to a German prince staying at a resort in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Youghal is a seaside town in County Cork, long a holiday destination.

clue.text: Welcome ending for Cthulhu in Weird Tales

indicators.note: one thing in another means it is put inside it
weird means strange or distorted, so these letters are mixed up
the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A reception for the closing of a Lovecraft monster story in the pulp magazine Weird Tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Weird Tales was the American pulp magazine where Lovecraft's Cthulhu stories appeared. 'Weird' rearranges TALES to SALTE, into which goes U.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to greet or welcome them with a gesture.

clue.text: Vampire free of Saturn after invasion of Earth

indicators.note: an invader gets inside, so this letter is put within the others
letters set free are released from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vampire liberated from the planet Saturn after an alien invasion of Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges OF SATURN to NOSFRATU; 'invasion of' then puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Orlok of the 1922 silent film is the screen's most famous early vampire, and the film's title names him.

clue.text: Short creep with large head

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to skulk is to creep about furtively

explanation.surface: A brief sneaky character with a big head.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull is the bony case of the head, so it stands for the head itself.

clue.text: Black magic is only half used in hospital

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
art can mean magic, as in the black art

indicators.note: using only half of a two-letter word means keeping one letter, here the second

explanation.surface: Dark sorcery being only partly practised inside a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black magic' looks like one phrase but splits into B and ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Barts is the familiar name for St Bartholomew's, a famous London hospital.

clue.text: It covers hair o' salt at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that protects the hair of an old salt while out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Headwear naturally covers the hair, and a mariner's cap is such an item.

clue.text: Place for swinging girls with scanty clothing? The reverse

indicators.note: clothing something means wrapping around it, one piece inside the other
the reverse means the containment runs the other way, so the girls wrap round the scanty piece

parts.note: gals are girls
low means scanty or meagre, as in low on supplies

explanation.surface: A spot for partying where young women wear skimpy outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinging' suggests partying, but it is hanging from a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The scaffold for hanging is where the condemned would swing, a grim euphemism.

clue.text: Lay person posing naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of coverings, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: a model is a person who poses for artists

explanation.surface: An ordinary person posing without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like the adjective meaning non-clergy, but it is a noun: a song or poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay is a short lyric poem or song, as is an ode.

clue.text: Fiendish types in Slough on the rampage

indicators.note: running wild means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Demonic figures running riot in the English town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, long mocked as dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghouls are evil spirits of folklore, fiends who rob graves.

clue.text: Cells embedded in Slovakia

indicators.note: something embedded is set inside, so the letters lie within this word

explanation.surface: Biological cells set in Slovakia.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs, the female reproductive cells, are what the plural Latin term denotes.

clue.text: Hold out what's needed for Saint Patrick briefly?

parts.words: what's needed for Saint Patrick briefly
parts.note: the short way of writing the saint's name needs the abbreviation for Saint, the word 'and', and the short form of Patrick

explanation.surface: Resisting change, wondering what is required to celebrate Ireland's patron saint quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Write Saint Patrick briefly as St and Pat and the three pieces join up.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse to change position or yield is the idiom's sense, like a poker player holding their cards.

clue.text: An Elizabethan magician is buried in India? That's right

indicators.note: buried in means placed inside, so these letters go within the others

parts.note: John Dee was Elizabeth I's astrologer and occultist

explanation.surface: Asking whether a court magician of Elizabeth I lies buried in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an emphatic agreement, much like saying 'quite so' or 'certainly'.

clue.text: 12 keeping Harry in shape

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: twelve o'clock is noon
to harry is to nag or harass

explanation.surface: A dozen people holding someone called Harry in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine-sided polygon is a geometric figure, a type of shape.

clue.text: Spread of Gaeldom after finally advancing here?

definitions.text: Spread of Gaeldom after finally advancing here?

indicators.note: a spread scatters things, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter is moved on one place in the alphabet, so the last letter becomes the next one

explanation.surface: Asking whether Irish-speaking culture has spread here after finally moving forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally advancing' turns the final M of GAELDOM into N, its successor in the alphabet; 'Spread of' rearranges GAELDON.
explanation.definitionFit: This county in Ireland's north-west has one of the largest Irish-speaking districts, where Gaelic culture is widespread.

clue.text: Unrelenting post-punk singer

definitions.meaning: unrelenting means refusing to change one's mind, firm
... was a British new-wave pop star of the early 1980s

explanation.surface: A stubborn musician from the era after punk rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and immovable in opinion is the adjective's meaning, and the singer's stage name happens to spell it.

clue.text: A Zamyatin novel not everyone finds dreadful

parts.note: We is Yevgeny Zamyatin's 1920s dystopian novel
some means a part, not everyone

explanation.surface: A Russian novel that some readers find terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense the word means inspiring dread or terror, so it fits dreadful.

clue.text: Jenny and I secure revolutionary period weapon

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast between them

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey, an ass

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Two people, Jenny and the speaker, acquiring an old weapon from a revolutionary era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' looks like a woman's name but is a female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a southern African spear, a slender throwing weapon.

clue.text: Girl entering Lady Stoneheart's house

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: A girl going into the home of Lady Stoneheart, the vengeful undead figure from A Song of Ice and Fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl entering' looks like the definition and the wordplay's start, but 'entering' is part of the string that 'house' holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl in crossword convention.

clue.text: Farmhouse needing 50% of capital upfront, extending into the future

indicators.note: upfront means at the front, so this piece leads
half of a six-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: London is the UK capital
a grange is a farmhouse with outbuildings

explanation.surface: A farmhouse purchase needing half the money paid in advance, with a long-term outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast that covers a distant period is one reaching far ahead in time.

clue.text: Laid-back attempt at humour with original approach

indicators.note: laid back means set going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a pun is a play on words, a try at a joke
ur- is a prefix meaning original, as in Urtext

explanation.surface: A relaxed attempt to be funny using a fresh approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid-back' looks like relaxed but signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The period leading up to an event, or the run before a jump, is its approach.

clue.text: Tony Soprano shot a fighter

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The TV mob boss shooting a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Soprano, the TV mob boss, is just Tony plus S for soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson, the heavyweight boxing champion, is a famous fighter.

clue.text: Hammer Night horror

indicators.note: to hammer is to batter something out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frightening night film from Hammer, the British horror studio.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammer Films was a British studio famous for horror.
explanation.definitionFit: The monster of the Carpenter film is a horror, a frightful creature.

clue.text: A new god? Wrong! It's an ancient one

indicators.note: wrong means put incorrectly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the article a, N as the abbreviation for new, and the word god as written

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a newly proposed deity, saying the actual one is old.
explanation.walkthrough: Dagon is a Philistine deity, and the title of a Lovecraft story.
explanation.definitionFit: Dagon was a god of the ancient Philistines, so he is an ancient deity.

clue.text: Aging fan gets involved in combo

indicators.note: becoming involved in something means getting inside it

parts.note: a combo is a small band, a group
a wing, like a fan, beats the air

explanation.surface: An older supporter joins a band.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting older is maturing, the gradual process of becoming an adult.

clue.text: Evil Clergyman at last is back

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse
at last points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An evil clergyman finally returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the last letter of 'Clergyman' together with 'is'. The Evil Clergyman is a Lovecraft story.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness or wrongdoing is the noun sense of evil, as in sin.

clue.text: 1980s film contracted Rod Steiger to play Tesla

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a pole is a rod

indicators.note: letters at play move about freely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the SI unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: Hiring the actor Rod Steiger to portray the inventor Nikola Tesla.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play' rearranges STEIGER to TERGEIS. 'Tesla' looks like the inventor but is the unit with symbol T.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1982 haunted-house movie produced by Spielberg is the 1980s film meant.
